name: layer_describe
description: One immutable JSON descriptor for DECLARED image sources: an E01/S01/Ex01 set's segments, the segments of a split raw image, or a virtual disk (VMDK, VHD, VHDX, QCOW) with the files it depends on, plus a sector size (a multiple of 512; 512 and 4096 both work). Nothing outside the declared list is looked for, listed or opened, and nothing is mounted. Each source is opened without waiting and without following a link (a symbolic link, FIFO, directory or device is refused), its size and sha256 are taken (sha256 is a custody fact; hash_sources false or a spent hashing budget gives not_hashed with the reason), and its container is named from its bytes. An EWF set is checked against its naming run and the chain of section descriptors of each E01/S01 segment is read here (a segment not declared, or a last declared segment that does not end the set, is a missing dependency); a split raw set is the declared files in the declared order and the media is the sum of their sizes; a QCOW2 backing file, a VMDK descriptor's parent and extents and a VHD differencing disk's parent are read from the headers and must be among the declared sources (matched by name), otherwise they are missing_dependencies and the programs are NOT run on that disk, because they would look for the file by name outside what was declared. A VHDX parent locator is not read and AFF is not examined, and the answer says so. With the sources whole, ewfinfo, qemu-img info --output=json (never --backing-chain, which can open files outside the evidence), img_stat, mmls and fsstat are run through the shared process block, each bounded, their whole output kept in content-addressed files, the sector size passed as -b. The partition table is true (mmls read one), false (mmls ran and recognised none, which does not show there is none) or unknown; each allocated slot (or the whole media when there is no table) is read with fsstat at its offset in sectors. The descriptor is canonical JSON with no clock in it, written as layer-<sha256 of its bytes>.json (mode 0600, created with a link so that an existing file is never replaced): the same inputs give the same bytes and the same name, and a second call says it was already there. It holds the declared paths exactly as given, because a consumer must open them; it is a private file, and the answer prints every path through the shared withholding. status is complete only when every declared source was read (and hashed unless declined), nothing declared is missing, the media size is known and agrees across what reports it, mmls ran to an answer and every allocated slot was read by fsstat; an undeclared dependency, a missing or timed-out program, a refused file system, an unreadable table row or a spent budget is partial with the reason; a refused or unreadable source, a set out of order or damaged and a mixed set are failed. Not measured: snapshots, that a file system fsstat reads is intact or unencrypted, that a source is the evidence it is said to be, and the section chain of an EWF2 segment (an EWF2 set is never complete). Dissect's target-query is not used. Not verified against the real programs: the qemu-img JSON keys it reads (format, virtual-size, backing-filename) are the ones qemu documents, qemu-img was not installed where this was tested, and the VMDK, VHD and QCOW header readers were tested on headers built from the formats' layouts, not on files a hypervisor wrote; the Sleuth Kit and libewf were run over raw, split raw and E01 sets. A SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP ends the program it was running and gives one JSON answer (partial, interrupted). A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 2: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape.

sources.description: The declared sources, in order (1 to 10000 paths): the E01 set's segments in naming order, the raw segments in order, or the virtual disk first and then the files it depends on. A file a header names that is not in this list is a missing dependency.

sector_size.description: The sector size in bytes, a multiple of 512 from 512 to 65536 (default 512); passed to img_stat, mmls and fsstat as -b and written in the descriptor.

hash_sources.description: Take the sha256 of each source (default true). At most 40 percent of the time budget goes to it; a source not reached is not_hashed with the reason.

out_dir.description: The directory for the descriptor and the programs' output files (default: layer_describe beside the tool's other output; it may already hold earlier descriptors, which are never replaced). In a job it must lie under $OUT: give {OUT}/<name>.

max_seconds.description: Time budget in seconds, 5 to 1700 (default 1500), inside the manifest's 1800.

limit.description: Source, partition and program rows in the inline answer, 1 to 5000 (default 200); the descriptor file holds every one.
